competitors.name: GitHub Native UI
what_they_do_well: Ubiquitous — every GitHub user knows it, zero adoption friction
Rich PR review experience with inline comments, suggestions, and multi-line diffs
Code scanning/Dependabot/secret scanning alerts surfaced directly in Security tab
Actions tab provides workflow run visualization with log streaming
Branch protection rules and required status checks are first-class
what_they_do_poorly: No cross-repo aggregation — security alerts scattered across individual repos
Alert triage is purely list-based, no queue/priority/assignment workflow
No provider-agnostic operating picture — GitHub-only worldview
Rich text editing in issues/PRs is limited, no structured evidence linking
No governed agent integration — Copilot chat is disconnected from security posture
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Do not copy GitHub's fragmented multi-tab UX. Rig Relay's differentiator is unified cockpit, not broader API coverage.
Single-vendor lock-in worldview — GitHub is the center of gravity, not the universe
List-based alert UI without triage state machine — users drown in unfiltered alerts
Siloed per-repo security posture — no organizational risk aggregation
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Cross-repo, cross-org security posture aggregation with governed evidence
Structured receipt-backed findings that survive beyond a single alert lifecycle
Multi-provider consultation (Council) before acting on security signals
Gated mutation proposals with adoption-approval workflow — GitHub can't gate itself
Content-light telemetry that proves what happened without leaking what was there
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay collapses N repo security tabs into a single cockpit with triage queues, risk summaries, and governed action — GitHub UI requires clicking through every repo individually.
competitors.technical_wedge: Receipt-backed append-only evidence graph (JSONL) vs GitHub's ephemeral alert list. Council adversarial review before mutation vs GitHub's single-model suggestions.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay is local-first, zero-trust on GitHub data — procurement can verify every action with receipts without trusting a SaaS vendor's audit log.

competitors.name: GitHub CLI
what_they_do_well: Scriptable GitHub operations from terminal — gh pr, gh issue, gh release
Pipeline-friendly — CI/CD integration via gh CLI in Actions workflows
Extension ecosystem — gh extension install for community tooling
JSON output mode for programmatic consumption
Auth management via gh auth login with device flow
what_they_do_poorly: No cross-repo aggregation — every operation is single-repo scoped
No security alert ingestion or triage — gh only surfaces basic issue/PR data
No governed agent integration — CLI is human-operated, not agent-callable with gating
No evidence chain — operations produce no receipts, no audit trail beyond GitHub audit log
Rate-limit awareness is manual — no budget enforcement, no graceful degradation
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Single-repo-scoped CLI model — Rig Relay must aggregate across repos/orgs
Human-only operation model — Rig Relay agents need governed programmatic access
No receipt/evidence model — every Rig Relay operation must produce a receipt
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Governed agent-to-GitHub bridge with per-operation permission gating
Receipt-backed evidence for every GitHub API interaction
Rate-limit budgeting across orgs with graceful degradation
Content-light telemetry that proves interaction fidelity without leaking data
Multi-repo portfolio operations (e.g., audit all repos for branch protection gaps)
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay cockpit shows what the agent can/should do on GitHub with one glance — gh CLI requires knowing every command and flag.
competitors.technical_wedge: Agent-operation gating with HMAC-signed receipts vs gh CLI's raw API access. Rate-limit budget per-org vs gh CLI's blind rate-limit consumption.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Every GitHub interaction is receipted and auditable locally — procurement doesn't need to trust GitHub's audit log or the agent's intentions.

competitors.name: GitHub Copilot (coding agent/workspace direction)
what_they_do_well: In-editor code completion with low latency and high accuracy
Copilot Chat with workspace context awareness
Copilot Workspace for multi-file task planning and execution
Agent mode with terminal access and file I/O
Deep VS Code/JetBrains integration with inline suggestions
what_they_do_poorly: No security alert awareness — Copilot doesn't know about CodeQL/Dependabot findings in the repo
No governed mutation — Copilot writes files directly, no adoption-approval gates
No receipt-backed evidence — no way to audit what Copilot did and why
Single-provider lock-in — only OpenAI models, no Council adversary review
No cross-repo context — Copilot sees one workspace, not the organizational security posture
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Do not copy Copilot's opaque agent behavior, permission overreach, or lack of auditable agent-action provenance.
Un-gated mutation — Rig Relay must never write files without governed approval
Single-provider dependency — Rig Relay's Council requires multi-provider adversarial review
Security-blind code generation — Rig Relay agents must consume security posture before acting
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Rig Relay is not primarily an in-editor autocomplete replacement. It is a governed GitHub operating and evidence layer that controls agent access, produces auditable receipts, and provides permission transparency.
Security-aware coding — agent consumes CodeQL/Dependabot/secret scanning alerts before proposing changes
Governed mutation with adoption-approval gates and SHA-verified receipts
Multi-provider Council review before mutation — Copilot uses a single model
Receipt-backed evidence chain for every agent action
Cross-repo security posture informs agent behavior across the portfolio
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay shows the security posture alongside the code — Copilot shows the code but is blind to the security alerts on the same repo.
competitors.technical_wedge: Council adversarial review + HMAC-signed adoption receipts vs Copilot's single-model, no-gate code generation. Security-aware context assembly vs workspace-only context.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay proves every code change was reviewed, gated, and receipted — Copilot provides no auditable evidence of what it did or why.

competitors.name: GitHub Advanced Security / CodeQL
what_they_do_well: Deep semantic analysis via CodeQL queries — finds vulnerabilities that pattern matchers miss
PR-integrated scanning — alerts surface inline in code review
Custom query support for organization-specific security policies
SARIF output for standardized alert interchange
Default query packs cover OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25
what_they_do_poorly: No cross-repo aggregation — alerts are per-repo, no organizational risk dashboard
Alert triage is binary (dismiss/open) — no priority, assignment, or lifecycle state machine
No governed remediation — alerts sit until a human acts, no agent-assisted fix proposal
Expensive per-seat licensing for Advanced Security — only available on GitHub Enterprise
No evidence chain linking alert → investigation → fix → verification
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Per-repo alert siloing — Rig Relay must aggregate across repos/orgs
Binary alert lifecycle (open/dismissed) — Rig Relay needs triage state machine
Expensive per-seat licensing model — Rig Relay is local-first, no per-seat fees
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Rig Relay does not replace CodeQL's semantic analysis. It complements, aggregates, and correlates GHAS signals and provides governed remediation and evidence. It should not claim to replace CodeQL unless it implements equivalent static analysis.
Cross-repo CodeQL alert ingestion with priority-based triage queues
Agent-assisted fix proposals gated by Council adversarial review
Receipt-backed evidence chain: alert → investigation → proposal → adoption → verification
Multi-provider analysis — Council can cross-reference CodeQL findings with other scanners
Content-light telemetry that proves alert handling fidelity without leaking vulnerable code
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay shows all CodeQL alerts across repos in one triage queue with governed action buttons — GitHub UI shows one repo at a time with no action workflow.
competitors.technical_wedge: Alert → fix evidence chain with HMAC receipts vs GitHub's binary open/dismiss lifecycle. Council multi-model review of proposed fixes vs single-model suggestions.
competitors.procurement_wedge: No per-seat licensing for security alert management — Rig Relay is free and local. Procurement gets auditable evidence of every alert handled, not just GitHub's audit log.

competitors.name: Dependabot
what_they_do_well: Automatic dependency update PRs with changelog and compatibility scores
Vulnerability-triggered alerts with severity ratings and CVE links
Grouped version updates to reduce PR noise
Ecosystem coverage: npm, pip, Maven, NuGet, Go modules, cargo, etc.
Configurable via dependabot.yml with schedule, labels, reviewers
what_they_do_poorly: No cross-repo dependency posture — each repo's dependencies are siloed
Alert fatigue — high volume of low-severity alerts, no intelligent triage
No governed merge — Dependabot PRs auto-merge or sit, no adoption-approval workflow
No organizational risk scoring — can't ask 'what's our most vulnerable dependency across all repos?'
No evidence chain linking vulnerability → risk assessment → fix → verification
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Alert-fatigue model — Rig Relay must prioritize and triage, not just list
Un-governed auto-merge — Rig Relay must gate dependency updates with adoption approval
Single-repo silo — Rig Relay must provide cross-repo dependency posture
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Cross-repo dependency vulnerability aggregation with organizational risk scoring
Governed dependency update proposals with Council adversarial review
Receipt-backed evidence chain: vulnerability → risk assessment → proposal → adoption → verification
Multi-scanner cross-referencing — Council can compare Dependabot findings with Snyk/OSV
Content-light telemetry proving dependency posture assessment without leaking dependency trees
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay shows your most critical dependency across all repos in one cockpit card — Dependabot shows hundreds of alerts scattered across repos.
competitors.technical_wedge: Cross-repo dependency risk scoring + governed adoption gates vs Dependabot's per-repo alert list. Council multi-scanner correlation vs single-source dependency data.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Procurement gets a single organizational dependency risk score with auditable evidence — Dependabot provides per-repo vulnerability lists with no organizational view.

competitors.name: SonarQube / SonarCloud
what_they_do_well: Comprehensive code quality metrics: bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells, coverage, duplications
Quality Gate enforcement — builds fail if quality threshold not met
Multi-language support with deep language-specific analyzers
Historical trend analysis with project quality evolution
PR decoration with inline issue annotations
what_they_do_poorly: Heavy on-prem installation (SonarQube) or SaaS vendor lock-in (SonarCloud)
No governed remediation — issues are reported, but no agent-assisted fix workflow
Quality Gates are binary (pass/fail) — no risk-based graduated enforcement
No cross-tool correlation — SonarQube doesn't correlate findings with CodeQL, Semgrep, etc.
Expensive enterprise licensing — additional cost beyond GitHub Advanced Security
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Heavy on-prem/SaaS deployment model — Rig Relay is local-first
Binary pass/fail quality gates — Rig Relay needs risk-based graduated enforcement
Closed-source, single-vendor analysis — Rig Relay should aggregate across scanners
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Aggregate SonarQube findings alongside CodeQL/Semgrep/Dependabot in one cockpit
Agent-assisted fix proposals with Council adversarial review before mutation
Receipt-backed quality evidence chain: finding → proposal → adoption → re-scan
Risk-based graduated enforcement (not binary pass/fail) with calibration over time
Content-light telemetry proving quality posture without leaking source code
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay shows quality posture from all scanners in one cockpit — SonarQube shows its own findings in isolation.
competitors.technical_wedge: Multi-scanner aggregation with calibrated risk scoring vs SonarQube's single-analyzer model. Governed mutation with adoption gates vs SonarQube's report-only workflow.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay is free and local — SonarQube Enterprise costs per-line/per-seat. Procurement gets multi-scanner evidence in one auditable system.

competitors.name: Semgrep
what_they_do_well: Pattern-based scanning with intuitive rule syntax — easier than CodeQL for custom rules
Fast scanning — runs in seconds, integrates into pre-commit and CI
Community rule registry with thousands of pre-built rules
Supply chain scanning (Semgrep Supply Chain) for dependency vulnerabilities
Secrets detection (Semgrep Secrets) with validation
what_they_do_poorly: Pattern-based analysis is shallower than CodeQL's semantic analysis for complex vulns
SaaS pricing for Semgrep AppSec Platform — local CLI is free, but management requires SaaS
No governed remediation — findings are reported, no agent-assisted fix workflow
No cross-tool correlation — Semgrep doesn't integrate with CodeQL/Dependabot findings
Alert management is basic — list view with status, no triage state machine
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: SaaS-required management plane — Rig Relay must be fully local-first
Pattern-only analysis limitation — Rig Relay should aggregate deeper analyzers too
Basic alert list without triage workflow — Rig Relay needs state-machine triage
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Semgrep findings ingested alongside CodeQL/Dependabot in one governed cockpit
Agent-assisted fix proposals with Council adversarial review
Receipt-backed evidence chain linking Semgrep finding → proposal → adoption → verification
Cross-scanner correlation — Council can verify Semgrep findings against CodeQL dataflow analysis
Content-light telemetry proving pattern coverage without leaking rule logic
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay shows Semgrep findings next to CodeQL/Dependabot in one triage queue — Semgrep AppSec shows its own findings in isolation.
competitors.technical_wedge: Multi-scanner evidence aggregation with Council correlation vs Semgrep's single-scanner view. Governed mutation pipeline vs Semgrep's report-only workflow.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay is free and local with no SaaS dependency — Semgrep requires AppSec Platform subscription for team management.

competitors.name: Qodana
what_they_do_well: JetBrains IDE inspection parity — same inspections you see in IntelliJ, now in CI
Language-specific deep inspections for JVM, .NET, PHP, Python, Go, JS/TS
License compliance checks for dependency licenses
PR annotation with inline issue markers
Cloud-based result aggregation across branches
what_they_do_poorly: JetBrains ecosystem lock-in — inspections are JetBrains-proprietary, not open standards
SaaS-only result aggregation — no local-first management plane
No governed remediation — findings are reported, no agent-assisted fix workflow
No cross-tool correlation — Qodana doesn't integrate with CodeQL/Semgrep findings
Limited language coverage outside JVM/IntelliJ-supported languages
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Single-vendor, proprietary inspection lock-in — Rig Relay must aggregate across tools
SaaS-only management plane — Rig Relay must be local-first
No governed remediation workflow — findings without action are noise
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Qodana findings ingested alongside other scanners in one governed cockpit
Agent-assisted fix proposals with Council adversarial review
Receipt-backed evidence chain linking Qodana finding → proposal → adoption → verification
Cross-scanner correlation — Council can verify Qodana code smells against Semgrep patterns
Content-light telemetry proving inspection coverage without leaking source code
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay shows Qodana findings next to CodeQL/Semgrep in one triage queue — Qodana shows its own findings in isolation.
competitors.technical_wedge: Multi-scanner evidence aggregation with governed mutation vs Qodana's single-scanner report. Local-first architecture vs Qodana's SaaS dependency.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay is free and local — Qodana requires Cloud subscription for team result aggregation. Procurement gets multi-scanner evidence in one system.

competitors.name: Sider / SideCI
what_they_do_well: Multi-tool aggregation — runs multiple linters/analyzers in one CI integration
PR-centric workflow — results surface inline in code review
Auto-correction suggestions for simple linting issues
Team-level configuration with shared rule sets
Historical trend analysis for code quality metrics
what_they_do_poorly: Discontinued/limited active development — SideCI shut down, Sider pivoted
SaaS-only delivery — no local-first operation
No governed remediation — auto-fix suggestions have no adoption-approval gates
No security alert correlation — aggregates linters, not CodeQL/Dependabot
No agent integration — human-only triage, no governed agent assistance
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: SaaS-only delivery with vendor continuity risk — Rig Relay must be local-first and open-source
Auto-fix without adoption gates — any mutation must pass governed approval
Linter-only aggregation without security scanner integration
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Multi-tool aggregation with security scanners (CodeQL, Dependabot, Semgrep) plus linters
Governed mutation pipeline with adoption-approval gates for any proposed fix
Receipt-backed evidence chain for every tool finding → proposal → adoption
Council adversarial review before any mutation is applied
Local-first, open-source architecture with no vendor continuity risk
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay aggregates linters AND security scanners in one governed cockpit — Sider aggregated linters only, and it's dead/in-pivot.
competitors.technical_wedge: Governed mutation + Council review + receipt-backed evidence vs Sider's report-and-suggest model. Local-first + open-source vs SaaS-only with vendor risk.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay is free, open-source, local-first — no vendor risk. Sider's discontinuation proves the SaaS-tool-aggregator procurement risk.

competitors.name: Linear (GitHub issue workflows)
what_they_do_well: Blazing-fast issue tracking with keyboard-first UX
Project/cycle planning with clear roadmap visualization
GitHub issue sync — Linear ↔ GitHub bidirectional bridge
Triage state machine with priority, assignee, status, and SLA tracking
Team velocity and cycle time analytics
what_they_do_poorly: No security alert integration — Linear tracks issues, not CodeQL/Dependabot findings
No governed agent integration — Linear is human-operated, no agent action pipeline
SaaS-only — no local-first operation, data lives on Linear's servers
No evidence chain — issues have statuses but no cryptographic receipts
No code scanning workflow — Linear doesn't understand code, only issues
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: SaaS-only delivery — Rig Relay must be local-first, data on user's machine
Issue-tracking-only worldview — Rig Relay must bridge issues to code to security posture
Human-only operation without governed agent integration
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Issue tracking integrated with security posture — issues linked to CodeQL/Dependabot findings
Governed agent response queue — agents can propose fixes for issues with Council review
Receipt-backed evidence chain: issue → investigation → proposal → adoption → verification
Local-first operation with no external SaaS dependency for issue data
Content-light telemetry proving issue handling fidelity without leaking issue content
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay links issues to security posture and enables governed agent action — Linear is a beautiful issue tracker blind to code and security.
competitors.technical_wedge: Issue-to-security-posture graph with governed mutation vs Linear's pure issue tracking. Cryptographic receipts vs Linear's status field. Local-first vs SaaS.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay keeps issue data local — no third-party SaaS access to your issue content. Procurement gets auditable evidence of issue resolution.

competitors.name: Backstage (software catalog patterns)
what_they_do_well: Unified software catalog — services, APIs, documentation, ownership in one place
Plugin architecture with extensive ecosystem (TechDocs, Kubernetes, CI/CD plugins)
Developer portal with self-service scaffolding (Software Templates)
TechDocs — documentation-as-code with MkDocs rendering
CNCF graduated project — broad community and enterprise adoption
what_they_do_poorly: Heavy operational burden — requires dedicated platform engineering team to run
No security alert integration — catalog shows services, not their CodeQL/Dependabot posture
No governed agent integration — Backstage is a portal, not an agent control plane
Passive catalog — shows what exists, doesn't enable governed action on it
Plugin quality varies wildly — many plugins are unmaintained or buggy
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Heavy operational burden requiring dedicated platform team — Rig Relay must be self-serve
Passive catalog without governed action — Rig Relay must enable action, not just display
Plugin fragmentation — Rig Relay should have a coherent, tested integration surface
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Software catalog with embedded security posture per service — Backstage shows ownership, Rig Relay shows risk
Governed agent action from catalog — find a service, see its risk, trigger agent investigation
Receipt-backed evidence for every catalog-linked action
Local-first, zero-ops — no platform engineering team required to run
Multi-provider Council review scoped to individual catalog services
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay's catalog shows what you own AND what's at risk with one-click governed action — Backstage shows what you own but not what's at risk.
competitors.technical_wedge: Security-aware catalog with governed mutation vs Backstage's passive catalog. Local-first zero-ops vs Backstage's platform-team-required deployment.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay requires zero dedicated platform engineering headcount — Backstage typically requires 1-3 FTEs. Rig Relay is free, Backstage has hidden operational cost.

competitors.name: CI Dashboard Tools (generic)
what_they_do_well: Build/test/deploy pipeline visualization across CI providers
Historical build metrics: pass rate, duration, flakiness
Alerting on pipeline failures with notification integrations
Multi-provider aggregation — GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CircleCI, GitLab CI
Team-level pipeline health dashboards
what_they_do_poorly: No security posture integration — CI dashboards show builds, not CodeQL/Dependabot findings
No governed agent integration — dashboards are view-only, no agent action pipeline
No evidence chain — build results are ephemeral, no cryptographic receipts
Passive monitoring — alerts on failure but no governed remediation workflow
Siloed from code review and issue tracking — build health in one place, code in another
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: View-only passive monitoring — Rig Relay must enable governed action on pipeline signals
Build-only worldview — Rig Relay must connect builds to security posture to code to issues
Ephemeral results without evidence chain — Rig Relay needs receipt-backed pipeline evidence
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: CI pipeline health integrated with security posture — failing build + open CodeQL finding in one cockpit card
Governed agent response to pipeline failures — agent investigates, proposes fix, Council reviews
Receipt-backed evidence for every pipeline interaction and agent response
Cross-repo pipeline health aggregation with security risk overlay
Content-light telemetry proving pipeline health monitoring fidelity
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay connects build failures to security posture and enables governed agent action — CI dashboards show a red square and wait for a human.
competitors.technical_wedge: Pipeline-to-security-to-code evidence graph with governed mutation vs CI dashboards' view-only build metrics. Cryptographic receipts vs ephemeral build logs.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay consolidates CI monitoring + security posture + governed remediation in one free, local tool — CI dashboards charge per-seat and don't remediate.

competitors.name: Release/Provenance Tools (generic)
what_they_do_well: SLSA provenance generation for build artifacts
SBOM generation (SPDX, CycloneDX) for dependency transparency
Sigstore/cosign integration for artifact signing
Attestation verification in CI/CD pipelines
Supply chain integrity: tamper-evident build pipelines
what_they_do_poorly: Build-time provenance only — no runtime evidence of what agents/code actually did
No agent action provenance — SLSA covers builds, not governed agent mutations
No security posture integration — provenance tools don't know about CodeQL/Dependabot findings
Heavy integration burden — requires pipeline reconfiguration and signing key management
No governed adoption workflow — provenance proves what was built, not whether it should be merged
what_rig_relay_should_not_copy: Build-time-only provenance — Rig Relay must provide runtime agent-action provenance
Heavy integration burden — Rig Relay should provide evidence with zero pipeline changes
Provenance without adoption governance — proving what was built is not enough
what_rig_relay_can_uniquely_do: Runtime agent-action provenance — every agent proposal, Council review, and mutation is receipted
End-to-end evidence chain: security finding → investigation → proposal → review → adoption → verification
Zero pipeline changes — Rig Relay produces evidence locally, no CI/CD reconfiguration
Governed adoption with cryptographic receipts — provenance + governance in one system
Content-light telemetry proving agent-action provenance without leaking code or secrets
competitors.ux_wedge: Rig Relay proves what agents proposed, reviewed, and adopted in one cockpit — provenance tools prove what was built but not who proposed it or why.
competitors.technical_wedge: Agent-action provenance + Council review receipts vs build-only SLSA provenance. Local-first zero-config vs pipeline-integration-heavy provenance tools.
competitors.procurement_wedge: Rig Relay provides both provenance AND governance — competitors provide provenance only. Procurement gets auditable evidence of every agent decision, not just build artifacts.
